claude-s · promo-video

Launch promos at 60 fps, with a cursor that moves like a hand

a 9 s promo for claude-s itself, 60 fps: show the cursor choreography and the silky motion, and prove the 60 fps claim on screen. Repo copy only, no reference's shots.

What the skill did

  • First video, claude-s · silk (9 s, 60 fps). On frame 0 the cursor is already in flight. It lands on Run on an ease measured off real demo videos (it eases off, then decays into the target), dwells, and presses. Run darkens and switches to Running instead of showing a click ring, and the cursor backs off.
  • Velocity-matched cuts at 1.5 s and 6.5 s: the outgoing shot speeds up into the cut, and the next one starts at the same speed in the same direction, then slows. The eye never loses the motion.
  • The cursor grabs the rail of the nine skills (their real demo titles and lengths from index.html); the card it holds lifts a little. It drags and lets go, and momentum carries the rail five cards to promo-video, which lifts. The fling gets 32 subframes, so the fast cards blur instead of ghosting.
  • A fair comparison: the left half is held on a 30 fps grid with no blur, and the right half is what render.mjs --smooth makes (60 fps, 180° shutter, blur averaged in linear light). Both halves draw faint ghosts at the frames they actually show.
  • The end card rises at the cut's speed. The cursor presses Copy on the README's clone command, the button turns orange and reads Copied, and the cursor fades. Measured on the MP4: judder index 0.006 (the smoothest X upload in the reference batch read 0.026). The motion check flags only the deliberate 30 fps half.
  • Second video, the Plexus launch promo (18 s): the brand from its repo, one primitive (a hub and its spokes) throughout, and the real UI redrawn inside one player frame that moves instead of cutting. Then a slot-list roll of real counts and a proof board of all 3,631 questions. Built with a banned list, a beat grid, a stills gate and two critique rounds.

Sound

  • silk: a 120 BPM groove from the first frame. A dark swell builds under Running and stops dead on the first whip, with a pass-by across it. The rail gets one tick per card crossing the centre, read off the rail's own motion, so the ticks slow down as it does. The beat before the comparison loses its bass, and half a second of silence comes before the end card, then an echo tail. Clicks stay silent; the label changes (Running, Copied) get a small pop.
  • Plexus: the mix stays low-passed under a dark build until "Mapped." lands. Every cut sits on a kick of a syncopated 120 BPM groove. There's foley for objects and silence for clicks, then half a second of silence and an echo tail on the logo.
